Thanks Marissa — got the PDF and skimmed the appendix. A couple of quick asks from our side before we route to procurement/legal: 

1) Uptime target: Skyline typically expects 99.99% for primary production services that handle PHI. Can you confirm whether Redwood can offer a higher-tier uptime for clinically-sensitive endpoints (we're open to an add-on pricing line)?

2) Maintenance blackout: we have a weekly maintenance blackout 08:00–12:00 ET Mon–Fri for certain clinical windows. We need assurance that any scheduled maintenance will not overlap those windows for endpoints flagged "clinical-prod". Can we add a clause to enforce regional blackout adherence?

3) Credits cap: procurement wants the cap increased from 30% to 50% for first-year safety assurance; legal prefers 30% but may take 40% as compromise.

Can your legal ops (cc'd) respond on acceptability of these three items and suggest language? If needed I can set up a 30-min call with our security and procurement folks.

Jordan — looping in legal ops. Quick responses inline below and I attached a short redline bundle (Skyline_OrderForm_v2_redlines.pdf) plus an executive summary spreadsheet (SLA_Redline_Summary.xlsx).

1) Uptime tier: We can offer an elevated "Clinical Prod" uptime tier at 99.99% as an optional addendum for endpoints that meet the defined scope (additional monthly fee applies). Suggested language: "Provider may offer an Elevated Uptime Tier (99.99%) for endpoints designated in writing as 'Clinical Prod'. Elevated Tier pricing and associated capacity reservation terms are set forth in Schedule A."

2) Maintenance blackout: Agreeable. Proposed clause: "Provider shall not schedule maintenance that impacts endpoints designated 'Clinical Prod' during Customer-specified blackout windows. Customer will provide a list of blackout windows at least 30 days prior to Effective Date and may update quarterly with 14 days' notice." This preserves operational flexibility while protecting Skyline's clinical windows. Note: this may require capacity reservations for those endpoints (see Schedule A).

3) Credits cap: We cannot accept a 50% cap as a standard; it materially alters risk allocation. Stated compromise in redline: year 1 cap = 40% with a defined escrow/rollback mechanism; thereafter revert to 30% unless Customer opts into Elevated Uptime Tier. Language added to Appendix B (see redline).
